case_number: Civil Appeal No. 2858 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) No. 16886 of 2019)
summary: The appellant challenged the employer's decision to treat his date of birth as 21st September 1945 for calculating VRS benefits, claiming it to be 21st September 1949, which would have entitled him to greater benefits due to longer service. The High Court and Division Bench rejected his plea. The appellant relied on his service book (1975), LIC policy (1980), and pay slips showing 21st September 1949, while the employer relied on Form 'B' under The Mines Act, 1952, showing 21st September 1945 and a medical report estimating his age as 25 years in 1971. A committee constituted in 2004 recommended acceptance of 21st September 1949 as the correct date, citing inconsistencies in initial record-keeping and reliance on non-statutory forms. The Supreme Court considered the principle of legitimate expectation and consistency in service records.
legal_provisions_cited: Durga Ram Vs. HCL, Case No. 2427/1990
Standing Orders of Khetri Copper Complex
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, and the appellant's date of birth was accepted as 21st September 1949 for the purpose of computing his VRS benefits, directing the employer to recalculate and release the outstanding dues accordingly.
